old_digest: Must not weigh less than five ounces and a half, and not more than five ounces and three quarters. At the beginning of each innings either party may call for a new ball.
new_digest: must not weigh less than five ounces and a half, nor more than five ounces and three quarters. At the beginning of each innings either may call for a new Ball.

old_digest: Shall stand at a reasonable distance behind the wicket and shall not move till the ball is out of the bowler’s hand; and shall not by any noise, incommode the striker; and, if his hands, knees, feet, or head, be over or before the wicket, though the ball hit it, it shall not be out.
new_digest: must stand at a reasonable distance behind the Wicket, and must not move till the Ball is out of the Bowler’s hand, not incommode the Striker by any noise; and, if his hands, knees, feet, or head, be over or before the wicket, though the ball hit it, it shall not be out.

old_digest: If the striker hits the other wicket, and his partner off his guard.
But, if the bowler’s foot is not behind the bowling-crease, and within the return-crease, when he delivers the ball, they must, unasked call no ball.
new_digest: The Umpires, in all matches, to pitch fair wickets, and the parties to toss for the choice of innings. But, if the bowler’s foot is not behind the bowling crease, and within the return crease, when he delivers the ball, they must, unasked call "no ball”.

old_digest: Must not exceed four inches and one quarter in the widest part.
new_digest: must not exceed four inches and a quarter in the widest part.

old_digest: Which are three, must be twenty-four inches out of the ground, the bails seven inches in length.
new_digest: must be twenty-four inches out of the ground, the bails seven inches in length.

old_digest: Must be opposite to each other, at the distance of twenty-two yards.
new_digest: must be opposite to each other, at a distance of twenty-two yards, which shall be pitched within thirty yards, fixed by the adversaries. It is not lawful for either party, during a match, without the consent of the other, to alter the ground by rolling, watering, covering, mowing, or beating. This is not meant to prevent the Striker from beating the ground with his bat, near where he stands, during the innings, or to prevent the bowler from filling up the holes, watering the ground, or using sawdust, when the ground is wet.

old_digest: Shall deliver the ball with one foot behind the bowling-crease, and within the return crease, and shall bowl four or six balls before he changes wickets, which he shall do but once in the same innings. He may order a striker at his wicket to stand on which side of it he pleases.
new_digest: shall deliver the ball with one foot behind the bowlingcrease, and within the return crease, and must bowl four balls before he changes wickets, which he is to do but once in the same innings.

old_digest: Shall have the choice of the innings, and the pitching of the wickets, which shall be pitched within thirty yards of a centre fixed by the adversaries. When the parties meet at a third place, the bowlers shall toss up for the pitching of the wickets and the choice of going in. It shall not be lawful for either party, during a match, without the consent of the other, to alter the ground by rolling, watering, covering, mowing, or beating. This rule is not meant to prevent the striker from beating the ground with his bat, near where he stands, during the innings, or to prevent the bowler from filling up the holes, watering his ground, or using sawdust, &c. when the ground is wet.
new_digest: must be bowled (not thrown or jerked), and delivered underhand, with the hand below the elbow. But if the ball be jerked, or the arm extended from the body horizontally, and any part of the hand be uppermost, or the hand horizontally extended when the ball is delivered, the Umpire shall call "No Ball". He may order the Striker, at his wicket, to stand on which side of it he pleases. If the bowler tosses the ball over the Striker's head, or bowls it so wide that the Striker cannot play at it, the party that is in shall be allowed one notch, to be put down to them, and those balls not to be reckoned in any of the four balls. If the bowler bowls a No Ball, the Striker may play at it, and be all ...

old_digest: If the bail is bowled off, or the stump bowled out of the ground; or If the ball, from a stroke over or under his bat, or upon his hand, (but not wrists) is held before it touches the ground, although it be hugged to the body of the catcher; or If in striking, or at any other time while the ball is in play, both his feet are over the popping-crease and his wicket put down; except his bat is grounded within it; or, If in striking at the ball he hits down his wicket; or, If under pretence of running a notch, or otherwise, either of the strikers prevent a ball from being caught, the striker of the ball is out; or If the ball is struck up, and either wilfully strike it again; or, If in running a ...

old_digest: If a striker is hurt some person may be allowed to stand out for him, but not go in.
new_digest: If a lost ball is called, the Striker shall be allowed four, but if more than four are run before "Lost Ball" is called, then the Striker to have all they have run. If a striker is hurt, some other Person may be allowed to stand out for him, but not go in.
